experience.title: Founder & Linguistic Lead — Murya (app.murya.ng)
experience.summary: Founded **Murya**, a Hausa speech synthesis and conversational platform live at [app.murya.ng](https://app.murya.ng). I lead its linguistic design and product and work with engineering to ship it:
bullets: **Speech synthesis:** an 8-speaker Piper VITS model at 22,050 Hz, fine-tuned on the WAXAL Hausa corpus and published as `adab-tech/murya-piper-hausa-tts` (weights CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; application code MIT). The demo names two of the eight voices, *Malama Asabe* (female) and *Malam Garba* (male). The app plays audio at 24 kHz, with under 110 ms to first audio in the browser.
**Tone:** syllable-weight segmentation (light CV vs heavy CVV/CVC) and right-to-left tonal melody mapping, following Litvinova, to guide Hausa pitch.
**Pragmatics:** Hausa politeness and respect norms (`Kunya & Girmamawa`), gendered address forms (`Namiji ka/maka vs Mace ki/miki`), and pedagogical tutor modes (`Malamin Hausa`).

**Ƙamus lexicon:** curated the 20,628-pair Robinson 1914 lexicon, published on Hugging Face (public domain), and obtained written permission from Prof. Paul Newman to use his 1977 *Modern Hausa–English Dictionary* internally (not redistributed) for dictionary-grounded lookup.
**Live voice:** real-time spoken conversation (Faster-Whisper speech recognition with echo suppression); dictionary and speech synthesis also work offline in the browser.

datasets.title: Mapping Voices: An Open Atlas of Oral-History and Voice-Testimony Collections
datasets.meta: Dataset (v0.4.0) · Zenodo · CC BY 4.0 · Creator & curator · [doi:10.5281/zenodo.22996478](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22996478)
datasets.description: Open research dataset and interactive atlas indexing 221 real, publicly documented oral-history and voice-testimony collections across 120 countries and territories and 125 languages. Persistent identifiers, controlled vocabularies (ISO 639-3, ISO 3166, UN M49), a published methodology, and an append-only review log; released as CSV, JSON, and GeoJSON with an interface in English, Hausa, French, and Arabic.
